item.title: Undefeated Middletown football team out of Section 9 final due to eligibility issue
item.description: Middletown has been removed from the Section 9 Class AA football playoffs after it was forced to forfeit its semifinal win due to an eligibility issue. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) An issue surrounding the use of an ineligible player has thrown the Section 9 Class AA football playoffs into chaos ahead of this weekend's sectional championships. Middletown, which boasted an undefeated record after its sectional semifinal win over Valley Central this past weekend, had been scheduled to face Newburgh Free Academy for the Section 9 title this coming Saturday, but has since forfeited that win for using an ineligible player. According to a letter posted to the Enlarged City School District of Middletown's website signed by superintendent Amy Creeden and athletic director Justin Sturge, in the aftermath of Middletown's 48-15 win over Valley Central, "a question was raised regarding whether one of our varsity football players met postseason eligibility requirements." After reviewing the situation with Section 9 officials, it was confirmed that the unidentified player did not meet the minimum requirement of participating in three regular-season games to be eligible for the postseason. The letter called the issue an "unintentional adult error in understanding the rules," and the district immediately requested a waiver from Section 9, which was denied. The district then appealed to the state high school athletic association, but the appeal was also denied. Due to the forfeit, Middletown's record has been dropped to 9-1 and Valley Central has been inserted into Saturday's Section 9 Class AA final against Newburgh. "We want to be very clear: this was an error made by adults, not our scholars," the letter reads. "Not one student-athlete did anything wrong." In a statement to the Times Union, NYSPHSAA Executive Director Robert Zayas said: "NYSPHSAA recognizes the disappointment and frustration surrounding the circumstances involving the Middletown varsity football program, particularly for the student-athletes who have worked hard throughout an outstanding season. "The rules and eligibility standards of NYSPHSAA are established and approved by our member schools through the Association's formal governance process. As Executive Director, my authority is defined by the NYSPHSAA Constitution and Handbook, and any exceptions to established rules must be consistent with the provisions approved by our membership. "While we recognize the circumstances surrounding this violation, NYSPHSAA has a responsibility to ensure the consistent and equitable application of its rules and eligibility standards across all member schools. According to the letter on the district website, the Middletown school district "is actively working with legal counsel to pursue further legal recourse on our team's behalf. item.title: Grade the trade: Vikings get a throwback QB, deal with Raiders for old friend Kirk Cousins
item.description: After Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings knew they had to try to get a quarterback. They landed a familiar face. The Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins, who spent six of his 15 NFL seasons in Minnesota. They sent a third-round pick to the Raiders for the 38-year-old quarterback, via ESPN . That should start the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas, while giving the Vikings hope for fixing their offense and winning the NFC North. Here are the grades for the trade: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins Usually, viable quarterbacks aren’t available in trade. Credit to the Vikings for getting a deal done. After Minnesota watched Carson Wentz flounder around on Monday night, and after the team realized Kyler Murray wouldn’t be the answer, a bold move was needed. Cousins has played pretty well this season, with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He can come right in and run Kevin O’Connell’s offense, which made him more valuable to Minnesota than some other teams. Kirk Cousins is coming back to the Vikings for a second stint with the team. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Thearon W. Henderson via Getty Images The Vikings weren’t going to be a Super Bowl contender with a treacherous quarterback situation. Cousins might not completely change that — he’s still by far the fourth-best quarterback in a tough division — but it’s well worth the price of a third-round pick to find out. Grade: B Raiders get a valuable pick The Raiders played the Kirk Cousins/Fernando Mendoza situation perfectly, as it turns out. They paid Cousins and gave him the first nine games of the season. With the Raiders slipping to 4-5 and their playoff hopes becoming more unrealistic, it was about time to turn the offense over to Mendoza anyway. So the Raiders paid for half of a season from Cousins and got a third-round pick out of it in the end. That’s really smart business. The Raiders might have Aidan O’Connell start for a few games if they truly don’t think Mendoza, the first overall pick, is ready. Either way, Las Vegas was playing chess with how it got a valuable top-100 pick for a 38-year-old quarterback who was probably going to start only a few more games anyway. Grade: A

item.title: Real Madrid eye 24-year-old Brighton ace as potential replacement for veteran superstar – report
item.description: Real Madrid eye 24-year-old Brighton ace as potential replacement for veteran superstar – report According to TeamTalk (h/t Bernabeu Digital ), Real Madrid have identified Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen as a potential replacement for veteran superstar Thibaut Courtois. The Spanish capital club are closely monitoring the Netherlands international’s progress as they begin planning for the long-term future of their goalkeeping position. Courtois still remains a key figure Courtois remains a key figure at Real Madrid and continues to be an important part of Jose Mourinho’s squad at the Santiago Bernabeu. At 34 years old, the Belgian shot-stopper continues to remain one of the best goalkeepers in the business. In the ongoing season, he has played 15 appearances across all competitions, keeping four clean sheets and conceding 16 goals. His performances have been clutch in the team maintaining an impressive run of form under Mourinho. Still a key figure at Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) While his current contract expires in 2027, a new one-year extension is already in the works for the veteran goalkeeper. However, Real Madrid are already laying the groundwork for life beyond their ace goalkeeper as they wish to be prepared with a succession plan rather than searching for a replacement when it becomes an immediate necessity. Bart Verbruggen the chosen one? As such, Real Madrid have identified Verbruggen as their most preferred candidate to take over from Courtois in the long run. The 24-year-old Dutchman’s age, physical presence, reliability between the posts and ability to contribute to build-up play make him an appealing option. Verbruggen’s contract expires in 2028. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Meanwhile, as per the report, the Netherlands goalkeeper would find it difficult to turn down a concrete offer from Real Madrid. However, the biggest obstacle for Los Blancos will be the position taken by Brighton & Hove Albion. They do not want to let go of the 24-year-old and see him as a key part of their project. But the summer of 2027 could provide a window of opportunity for Real Madrid. Verbruggen’s contract with the Seagulls expires in 2028, meaning he would be entering the final year of his deal at the end of the current season. If a new contract is not negotiated, he could become available for a reasonable price and Brighton could be forced to sell in order to avoid losing him for free when his deal runs out.

item.title: 49ers add wide receiver Keenan Allen in trade with Colts as deadline approaches
item.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen (10) catches a pass in front of Dallas Cowboys' Malik Hooker (24) andn Daron Bland (26) during the first half of an NFL football game in Indianapolis, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Jeff Roberson) (Jeff Roberson/Associated Press) On Tuesday, two weeks after the San Francisco 49ers acquired a 30-something from the Colts, they acquired another 30-something from Indianapolis in an all-in Super Bowl push. The 49ers traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts for wide receiver Keenan Allen, 34, after dealing a 2027 fourth-rounder to Indianapolis for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, 32, a league source said. The 49ers have five picks in next year's draft: a first-, second-, third-, fifth- and seventh-rounder. With the 49ers dealing with a host of wide receiver injuries, most notably to six-time Pro Bowl selection Mike Evans, they dealt for Allen, a six-time Pro Bowl pick who has 40 catches for 351 yards and a touchdown in eight games this season. Allen, a 14-year veteran who attended Cal, is an elite route-runner who ranks second among active players in receptions (1,095), fourth in receiving yards (12,402) and fifth in receiving touchdowns (71). Allen, of course, is in his career twilight. The 49ers will be his fourth team since he was traded from the Chargers to the Bears for a fourth-round pick in March 2024. Since his last Pro Bowl season in 2023, he has 191 catches for 1,872 yards and 12 touchdowns in 40 games, averaging 9.8 yards per catch. Sporting a 7-1 record, the 49ers grabbed Allen about two hours before Tuesday's 1 p.m. trade deadline with Evans, 33, dealing with Achilles tendinitis that's sidelined him since he was forced to exit a win against the Commanders on Oct. 19. item.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
item.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. No. 15 Oregon (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) hosts No. 23 UCLA (4-0, 2-0) at 12:30 p.m. on Oct. 10. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. item.title: Red Wings GM Admits He Is Fielding Calls on Simon Edvinsson
item.description: On Tuesday, Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff attended his first NHL general managers meeting in Toronto. He is still carrying two difficult situations into it: Dylan Larkin is suspended without pay after leaving the team on Oct. 29, and Simon Edvinsson is still an unsigned restricted free agent. Horcoff would still rather sign Edvinsson than move him. Asked whether the standoff could soften that position, he told Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com , “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls. It’s my job to do what’s in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings. I’m going to take all those calls and hear what people have to say.” Apr 11, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; New Jersey Devils left wing Brian Halonen (48) skates with the puck defended by Detroit Red Wings center Andrew Copp (18) and defenseman Simon Edvinsson (77) in the third period at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Simon Edvinsson Has Until Dec. 1 to Sign Edvinsson has until Dec. 1 to sign a new contract with the Red Wings, or he cannot play this season. Last season he scored nine goals and recorded 16 assists in 72 games , along with a plus-minus rating of 12. He is only 23 years old, and with the cap space available to Detroit , it would be a failure if the Red Wings can’t get a long-term deal finished. Edvinsson Keeps Skating in Nashville Edvinsson has been seen skating in Nashville twice, in a Red Wings jersey. He told Nick Kieser of Lower Broad Pucks that Predators forward Filip Forsberg recommended a local coach to him, and that he is still hoping for something to get done soon . Cotsonika also wrote that Edvinsson reportedly wants to be traded, which keeps the Predators a name worth watching before Dec. 1. What Happens if Edvinsson Does Not Sign If Edvinsson is not playing anywhere this season, it would be interesting to see where Horcoff would take things. He may have to trade him before Dec. 1 if Edvinsson does not want to be here, even though Horcoff would like to keep him around for the long haul.

item.title: Real Madrid star opens the door to January exit
item.description: Real Madrid star opens the door to January exit Real Madrid star Endrick has admitted that he has not yet ruled out the possibility of departing Spain’s capital on loan during the winter transfer window. This comes amid a fresh round of speculation surrounding the name of the Brazilian international. Frontman Endrick has reemerged as a prominent figure in the transfer chatter across much of Europe over the last 24 hours. Amid a search for mid-season reinforcements up top, Premier League champions Arsenal are understood to have earmarked the 20-year-old as a potential loan signing. Endrick has continued to struggle for game-time at Real Madrid this season, despite being repeatedly backed by manager José Mourinho in public. Speaking during an exchange with the media on Tuesday, the young attacker was himself therefore drawn on the prospect of a 2nd successive winter loan move. And Endrick, as cited by Fabrizio Romano, went on to inform Brazilian journalist Cahê Mota: “I’m only 20, so I’ll see how things unfold. I just want to play, be happy, and help my teammates. “I don’t know what will happen in January; that’s in God’s hands. I only ask for what’s best for my career. Whatever is meant to happen, will happen. I’ll keep my feet on the ground and continue doing my absolute best. Madrid is a wonderful city, but I will always do whatever it takes to advance my career.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Seattle Seahawks 2026 trade deadline tracker
item.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. item.title: 76ers Undefeated In Clutch, But This Streak Is A Trap
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers have won every single close game they have played this season, but that perfect record might be the biggest problem they face. The team improved to 9-2 on the season after beating the Chicago Bulls 127-121 on Sunday, a victory that kept their clutch record at a flawless 8-0. While fans love the drama, the reality is that a roster full of aging stars cannot survive this much stress week after week. The 76ers have played eight clutch games so far, which is the most in the entire league by a wide margin, according to The Sixer Sense . LeBron James has a clear explanation for why the team stays cool when the clock winds down. He told reporters after the win that the squad simply does not panic under pressure. “We have a lot of guys that’s been in late-game situations, and we have a no-panic button,” James said. He added that the group understands they must get stops, but they also know how to stay calm if the other team goes on a run. This mindset has worked so far, but it masks a deeper issue with how the team plays for the full 48 minutes. The Danger of Constant Comebacks Winning tight games is a great trait to have, yet relying on it every night is a recipe for exhaustion. According to The Sixer Sense , the 76ers have recovered from deficits to secure victories far too frequently this season, even versus inferior opponents. A team that does not dominate early will eventually run out of gas, and this roster is not exactly young across the board. Although the 76ers must leverage their talent edge earlier, they repeatedly allow contests to reach the last possessions for a winner to emerge. This pattern is dangerous for a group that includes players like James and Joel Embiid who need rest. Shooting Stars in the Final Minutes The stats show just how well the offense clicks when the pressure is highest. In clutch time, the Sixers are outscoring opponents 86-67 while shooting 52.2% from the field, according to Crossing Broad. Tyrese Maxey contributed significantly to that success by recording 30 clutch points on 6-of-11 shooting plus 15-of-17 from the line with no turnovers. LeBron James also contributed 22 points in the win over the Bulls, marking his highest-scoring game as a 76er. Even though the numbers look great, the fact remains that they should not need to rely on such high-pressure finishes to get Ws. The 76ers will need to find a way to start strong and keep that level of play for the whole game if they want to avoid burning out. The team has the firepower to put away opponents early, yet they keep finding themselves in tense moments when their talent suggests they should be winning by double digits. Now 8-0 in games extending to crunch time, the 76ers possess a perfect record that remains notable despite growing clarity about the dangers of this strategy.

item.title: Here’s What Malik Nabers Revealed After Fox Criticized His Attitude
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has entered a heated public dispute with Fox Sports broadcasters following the team’s 19-11 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. During the game, play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen criticized Nabers for his demeanor, with Davis stating the player’s body language “has been terrible today”. Nabers responded quickly on social media, taking to an Instagram story to call out the commentators for their assessment. Defending the Stoic Look The core of the argument centers on whether a player must show emotion to be a good teammate. Olsen had suggested that great receivers must demand the ball, noting, “There’s never been a great wide receiver who hasn’t demanded the ball”, according to ESPN . However, he also warned that being demanding should never hurt the team’s success. Nabers rejected the idea that his face changes based on the score. He insisted, “My face is the same way if I’m having a good game, bad, winning or losing”. Nabers clarified that his frustration was actually directed at his own team’s effort, not his teammates. He admitted he felt the offense was “lollygagging our way through the game”, according to Sports Illustrated . He explained that he was trying to “wake everybody up just to make sure we’re playing a game right now”. The receiver emphasized that in a division matchup, players must “go attack people, you have to go attack the game”. Coach Harbaugh Steps In Giants head coach John Harbaugh addressed the controversy during his media availability on Monday. He defended his player, pointing out that outsiders cannot see the full context of what happens on the field. item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs have played eight games, and the season now sits right in the middle. Arrowhead Pride staff members cast votes to pick the team’s most improved player for this point in the year. Nine writers from the outlet each had one vote to decide the winner among several candidates. Defensive back Chris Roland-Wallace won the award with four total votes. He beat out edge rusher Felix Anudike-Uzomah, who received three votes, while Ashton Gillotte and Nohl Williams each took one vote. Roland-Wallace joined the team as a rookie free agent from USC after the 2024 draft. He made the roster in a long-shot bid and quickly became a top special teams player. Grades and Snap Counts Rise Roland-Wallace started the season playing safety while Chamarri Conner recovered from a knee injury. Pro Football Focus gave him a 72.2 grade for his play at safety, which ranks 20th out of 100 players at the position. His coverage grade of 77.6 is even better, placing him sixth among all safeties in that metric. In run defense or open-field situations, he recorded 14 solo tackles. He allows an 84.6% completion percentage in the slot., he limits the damage by giving up only 6.4 yards per completion over eight games. His role grew bigger after veteran L’Jarius Sneed went on the Reserve/Injured list with a chronic knee injury. Roland-Wallace saw his defensive snap count jump above 70% in each of the last two weeks. The on-field results suggest he should keep that workload even if Sneed returns. He plays multiple roles and could build a decent career as a high-end backup for the franchise. Contract Future and Free Agency The Chiefs face a tough decision about Roland-Wallace after this season ends. He will become a restricted free agent (RFA) following the season. For the 2027 offseason, Over the Cap estimates the minimum RFA tender at $3.8 million. Because he went undrafted, Kansas City would not get any draft-pick compensation if he signs with another team. The Chiefs would have the right to match any offer, but other teams might sign him to a deal the Chiefs cannot match. The team is tight against the salary cap, so a modest extension might be the first move in the offseason. item.title: Red Sox Boss Gives Roman Anthony And Triston Casas The All Clear
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Red Sox fans watching the injury report now have news. Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow gave a clear update on Roman Anthony and Triston Casas at the GM Meetings in Las Vegas. The team knows both players are healing, and the 2027 season looks much brighter because of it. Breslow said Anthony is still resting but feels good. “I talked to him yesterday, he’s excited about what the offseason will bring,” Breslow said. Sprained right hand sidelined the young outfielder for nearly four months, and the injury was aggravated during the playoffs. Original diagnosis of an aggravated hand sprain alongside surrounding muscle irritation was confirmed by imaging, so surgery was unnecessary. Rest Is The Only Path Forward The plan for Anthony is simple and strict. He will not hit a ball until the doctors say he is fully ready. Breslow noted that at this point they’ve “taken every picture that one can take” of his hand to ensure no hidden issues remain. “Rest, that will be the most important part of the recovery process,” Breslow said. The team will evaluate him again in the next couple of weeks before he starts range of motion and strengthening exercises. This approach makes sense given the history. A partially torn ring finger CMC ligament caused Anthony to miss a chunk of the 2026 season. Pushing him too fast would be a mistake the front office cannot afford.
